summary: Tested Game Access & Visibility Controls (P0). Backend: 9/18 tests pass — public preview E2E, audit+rollback, registry, simulate, invalid-username validation, founder bypass, preview flag toggles, and Dragon Realm legacy migration to founder_only all work. However, 8 tests fail with the SAME root cause: a pre-existing platform-wide `games_play` ai_access_policy (invite_only=true, restricted=true) short-circuits ALL non-founder access to /api/games and /api/games/{gid} BEFORE the new per-game access_ctl runs. This makes Custom Users / Badge Access / Progression / View Only / Preview / Maintenance modes unreachable for real users (tftwo/auditcheckreal are 403'd upstream with a plain-string detail). Frontend admin panel (GameAccessPanel) renders and works; public /preview/game/{token} route renders with disclaimer + play button + runtime iframe as a guest.

critical.issue: Platform-wide check_access('games_play') gate in routers/games.py lines 278/320 blocks ALL non-founders (restricted=true, invite_only=true in ai_access_policies collection) BEFORE the new per-game access_ctl runs. Result: Custom Users, Badge Access, Progression, View Only, Preview, and Maintenance modes cannot grant any real user access; every non-founder gets 403 with `detail: 'OurRealm Games are in founder testing — access opens soon!'` regardless of what the founder configures in the new Access & Visibility panel. This defeats the P0 feature.

When check_access denies, `raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=pol['reason'])` returns detail as a PLAIN STRING. The new access_ctl and the frontend blocked-panel expect a structured `{reason, message}` object. Inconsistent error shape between the two enforcement layers.

integration_issues.flow: Normal user opens a game that's configured for their access mode (custom_users / badge_access / progression / view_only / preview)
integration_issues.issue: Backend upstream 403 (games_play policy) means the frontend GamesHub blocked panel / view-only overlay / access banner will never receive an access_ctl payload for non-founders — they'll see the generic 'founder testing' 403 message instead. Cannot be verified end-to-end until the backend blocker is fixed.

action_items: Reconcile the pre-existing platform-wide `games_play` ai_access_policy with the new per-game access_ctl. Recommended: in routers/games.py games_hub and play_game, skip/downgrade the check_access('games_play') gate when the game has an explicit `access` config that would allow the user, OR auto-add resolved usernames to games_play.allow_usernames when a founder saves a per-game access config, OR relax the games_play platform policy so per-game access_ctl becomes the effective gate.
Normalize the 403 detail shape across both enforcement layers — always return {reason, message} object so the frontend can render access_ctl-aware messaging.
Once the outer gate is unblocked, re-run test_game_access_ctl_iter123.py; the 8 currently failing assertions should all flip to green with no test-code changes needed.
critical_code_review_comments: Two overlapping enforcement systems (services/access_policy.py::check_access and services/game_access_ctl.py::evaluate) both gate the same endpoints. This is fragile and confusing — pick one authoritative gate for games or make the outer one a pre-filter that defers to per-game config when present.

game_access_ctl.evaluate() is well-structured (mode → filter → flags) and includes founder_bypass + trace; the code itself looks solid. Audit history includes `env_db` which is good for cross-env forensics.
public_preview route correctly disables all rewards, is properly whitelisted in global_auth_guard, and rate-limits per-IP at 40/min — nice.
normalize_config hard-locks flags to default_flags for view_only + public_preview even if the founder posts overrides — safety net working as spec (Public Preview MUST NEVER grant rewards).
put_access resolves usernames case-insensitively and rejects invalid ones with 400 — good validation. Deduping and @-stripping works.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: services/access_policy.py has a `games_play` feature entry, and the ai_access_policies MongoDB collection has {_id:'games_play', restricted:true, invite_only:true, message:'OurRealm Games are in founder testing — access opens soon!'}. routers/games.py `games_hub` (line ~278) and `play_game` (line ~320) call `check_access('games_play', current, consume=False)` BEFORE consulting services/game_access_ctl.py::evaluate(). Because tftwo/auditcheckreal are not on the platform-wide allow_usernames list and have no grants, they get 403 with a string detail every time, bypassing the entire new per-game access system. REPRODUCTION: as tftwo, GET /api/games/4559297f1ff54f789e4fb6fae9122473 → 403 with body {"detail":"OurRealm Games are in founder testing — access opens soon!"} regardless of whether the founder has set that game to custom_users:[tftwo] / view_only / preview / etc. MITIGATION options: (a) In games_hub/play_game, if game has explicit `access` config, call access_ctl.evaluate() FIRST and only fall back to check_access when it's a legacy game with no access config; (b) Auto-mutate games_play.allow_usernames when access_ctl grants a specific user; (c) Relax the platform games_play default. Simplest fix: swap the two gates or gate `check_access` behind `if not game.get('access')`.
